name: Augustus
info: Augustus, born Gaius Octavius and known as Octavian, was the founder of the Roman Empire and its first emperor from 27 BCE to 14 CE, whose principate opened the era of the Pax Romana.

facts.born: 23 September 63 BCE, in Rome, at a family property on the Palatine Hill; son of Gaius Octavius, of an equestrian branch of the gens Octavia, and Atia, niece of Julius Caesar
facts.died: 19 August 14 CE, at Nola, of natural causes at the age of 75; Tacitus and Cassius Dio claimed that his wife Livia poisoned him, which many historians dismiss
facts.role: Consul from 43 BCE; triumvir from 43 BCE; princeps and first Roman emperor, with the title augustus, from 27 BCE to 14 CE; pontifex maximus from 12 BCE; pater patriae from 2 BCE
facts.known: founding the principate; victory at Actium over Mark Antony and Cleopatra; the Pax Romana; the annexation of Egypt and wide conquests; the Res Gestae Divi Augusti; reform of taxation and the army; the Praetorian Guard; rebuilding Rome in marble

t: Named heir by his great-uncle Julius Caesar, Octavian used Caesar's money, name and veterans to win the civil wars that followed the assassination of 44 BCE.
From 27 BCE he kept the forms of the Republic while holding the army, half the provinces and a growing set of powers, a system known as the principate.
His reign brought conquests, a standing army, tax reform and a long peace, but it began with proscriptions and executions, and writers from Tacitus to Ronald Syme have judged it an autocracy.
dyk: The Roman month of Sextilis was renamed August after him in 8 BCE; he chose it because it was the month of his first consulship and of several of his victories.
ev: Julius Caesar is assassinated and his will names Octavius his main heir, with the condition that he take Caesar's name
Octavian marches on Rome, becomes consul at 19 and forms the triumvirate with Mark Antony and Lepidus
Antony and Octavian defeat Brutus and Cassius in two battles at Philippi
Agrippa defeats Antony and Cleopatra at the Battle of Actium
Antony and Cleopatra take their own lives and Egypt passes under Octavian's direct control
Octavian returns power to the Senate, takes back most provinces and receives the title augustus
After a severe illness he resigns the consulship and receives tribunician power for life
Augustus dies at Nola; he is succeeded by his stepson and adopted son Tiberius and deified by the Senate

sections.early:
Gaius Octavius was born in Rome on 23 September 63 BCE, at a family property on the Palatine Hill. His father, also Gaius Octavius, came from a moderately wealthy equestrian family of the gens Octavia from Velitrae, near Rome, rose through the cursus honorum and governed Macedonia; according to Suetonius the boy was given the cognomen Thurinus to commemorate his father's victory over followers of Spartacus at Thurii. His mother, Atia, was a niece of Julius Caesar. After his father died in 59 or 58 BCE, Atia married Lucius Marcius Philippus, consul in 56 BCE.

His first public appearance was the funeral oration for his grandmother Julia, Caesar's sister, in 52 or 51 BCE. A Greek slave tutor, Sphaerus, taught him reading, writing, arithmetic and Greek, and as a teenager he studied philosophy under Areios of Alexandria and Athenodorus of Tarsus and rhetoric under Marcus Epidius and Apollodorus of Pergamon. He grew up during the civil war between Caesar and Pompey. In 47 BCE, after he took the toga virilis, Caesar had him elected pontiff; poor health kept him from the African campaign, but in 45 BCE he joined Caesar in Hispania, and on 13 September 45 BCE Caesar deposited a will naming him principal heir.
sections.rise:
Octavius was at Apollonia in Illyria when Caesar was assassinated on 15 March 44 BCE. The will left him three-quarters of Caesar's estate on condition that he take Caesar's name; against his stepfather's advice he accepted, called himself Gaius Julius Caesar, and is known to historians as Octavian. He took 700 million sesterces stored at Brundisium for Caesar's Parthian war, seized the tribute of Asia without permission and, by June, had raised 3,000 veterans. He contested the leadership of the Caesarians with the consul Mark Antony, while Cicero attacked Antony in a series of speeches.

When Antony besieged Decimus Brutus at Mutina, Cicero had Octavian made a senator on 1 January 43 BCE with a legal command. Both consuls died in the battles of Forum Gallorum and Mutina, leaving Octavian with their armies. Denied the consulship, he marched on Rome and on 19 August 43 BCE, aged 19, became consul. In October he, Antony and Lepidus formed the triumvirate, legalised by the lex Titia. Their proscriptions outlawed some 300 senators and equestrians and confiscated thousands of properties, and in October 42 BCE they defeated Brutus and Cassius at Philippi. In the following years Octavian fought Lucius Antonius at Perusia and Sextus Pompey at sea, removed Lepidus in 36 BCE, and broke with Antony, who was allied with Cleopatra. Agrippa defeated them at Actium on 2 September 31 BCE, and in 30 BCE both took their own lives.
sections.deeds:
On 13 January 27 BCE Octavian publicly returned power to the Senate; three days later he accepted a ten-year charge over provinces that held most of the legions, and the Senate gave him the title augustus, "the revered". A second settlement in 23 BCE gave him greater proconsular power across the empire and the power of a tribune for life; he later added imperium in Rome itself, became pontifex maximus in 12 BCE and was named pater patriae in 2 BCE. Egypt, which he ruled through an equestrian prefect, was treated as his own property.

His armies conquered northern Hispania, Raetia, Noricum, Illyricum and Pannonia, annexed Galatia and extended Africa Proconsularis; Judea was added to the province of Syria. In 20 BCE he recovered from Parthia the standards lost by Crassus, and a treaty with Queen Amanirenas of Kush set the new border at Maharraqa. In Rome he created the Praetorian Guard in 27 BCE and the vigiles, a fire brigade and police force, in 6 CE, fixed a standing army of 28 legions of about 170,000 soldiers with a military treasury, replaced the tax farmers with salaried collectors and assessed taxes by census. He boasted that he found Rome a city of bricks and left it one of marble, raising the Ara Pacis, the Forum of Augustus and many temples, and was a patron of poets such as Virgil.
sections.opponents:
Octavian's rise was violent. Contemporary historians disagree which triumvir was most responsible for the proscriptions, but agree that all three used them to eliminate enemies. His veteran settlements evicted whole populations from some eighteen cities in Italy, and after Perusia surrendered in February 40 BCE he had 300 senators and equestrians executed on the anniversary of Caesar's death, reprisals that sullied his reputation; Propertius disapproved of the executions of prisoners. After Alexandria he had Caesarion, Cleopatra's son by Caesar, and Antony's son Antyllus killed.

Under the principate, the Marcus Primus affair of 23 BCE raised the charge that he had ordered a war in a senatorial province, which he denied under oath; some jurors seem to have disbelieved him. The conspirators led by Fannius Caepio were executed as soon as they were captured, without giving testimony, and he concealed these events. As triumvir he destroyed the public records from 44 to 36 BCE, and around 8 CE he exiled the poet Ovid. The jurist Marcus Antistius Labeo openly criticised his regime; Tacitus wrote that he cunningly reduced Republican Rome to slavery, and Cassius Dio, while calling him benign and moderate, saw him as an autocrat. Ronald Syme in The Roman Revolution (1939) called him a "sickly and sinister youth" whose faction resembled a crime syndicate.
sections.last:
The succession troubled Augustus from his illness in 23 BCE. His nephew Marcellus, married to his daughter Julia, died that year; Julia then married Agrippa, whose sons Gaius and Lucius Augustus adopted as heirs. Agrippa died in 12 BCE and Augustus made his stepson Tiberius divorce Vipsania to marry Julia; Tiberius's brother Drusus died in 9 BCE. Augustus exiled Julia for adultery in 2 BCE. After Lucius died in 2 CE and Gaius in 4 CE, he recalled Tiberius and adopted him in June 4 CE, on condition that Tiberius adopt Germanicus. He exiled his youngest grandson, Agrippa Postumus, and disowned him.

His last years brought hard news from the frontiers: an Illyrian revolt from 6 to 9 CE, and in 9 CE the destruction of three legions under Publius Quinctilius Varus by Arminius in the Teutoburg Forest, after which he advised against further conquest in Germany. In 8 CE he handed foreign embassies to three ex-consuls, and by 13 CE Tiberius held power equal to his. His health declined in the months before his death at Nola, where his father had died, on 19 August 14 CE. His reported last words asked whether he had played the part well. Tiberius and his son Drusus gave the eulogy, the body was cremated near his mausoleum, and the Senate deified him.
sections.legacy:
Augustus created a regime that kept relative peace and prosperity for two centuries, the Pax Romana or Pax Augusta, though the myth of an Augustan golden age may obscure the difficulties he faced. The principate lasted until the Crisis of the Third Century, and his regime laid foundations for the idea of universal monarchy in the Byzantine and Holy Roman Empires. The names Caesar and augustus became titles of Roman rulers for fourteen centuries, Caesar the root of kaiser and czar and imperator of "emperor". Later Romans wished each emperor after Trajan to be "more fortunate than Augustus and better than Trajan". His Res Gestae, copied throughout the empire, was called by Theodor Mommsen the "queen of inscriptions".

Church fathers such as Orosius and Bede presented him as a divinely ordained peacemaker for the coming of Christ, and Petrarch as a righteous ruler. Jonathan Swift, Montesquieu, Voltaire and Thomas Blackwell saw a usurper or tyrant; the 19th century more often a reformer. Benito Mussolini celebrated his bimillenary in 1937-1938, and Syme's work, written against that background, shaped scholarship in the English-speaking world. Werner Eck and Sarolta Takács credit him with a standing professional army, dynastic succession and long peace; Adrian Goldsworthy in 2014 called him essentially a military dictator, but no more ruthless than other warlords, and judged comparisons with modern dictators anachronistic.

summary: Augustus, born Gaius Octavius, rose as Julius Caesar's heir through civil war, proscriptions and the defeat of Antony and Cleopatra, and from 27 BCE ruled Rome as princeps behind republican forms. His reign of conquest, reform and building began two centuries of relative peace; ancient and modern critics have called it an autocracy.

notes: The article's Deification section dates the Senate's proclamation to '17 September 27 BC', which cannot be right for a deification after his death in AD 14; left the date out.
His exact words 'Acta est fabula, plaudite' paraphrased in 'last' rather than quoted.
The article gives no figure for the dead of the proscriptions beyond some 300 outlawed and 300 executed after Perusia.
Deification is placed in the 14 CE event without a date, as the article's own date is doubtful.
